stories.headline: Brent slips to [$91.97] as Hormuz attacks continue
stories.summary: Brent fell 0.65% to $91.97 a barrel and WTI fell 0.59% to $82.92 on Monday morning. Oversupply worries are weighing on prices. Weekend ship attacks in the Gulf near Hormuz, reported by UKMTO, limited the fall. Brent lost 4% last week. OPEC+ ministers meet on 29 November to discuss 2027 output.

stories.headline: Sea drones strike Russian ships in [Benghazi port]
stories.summary: Eastern Libya's government says a suspected sea drone attack hit a Russian vessel at Benghazi naval base, causing an explosion and a brief fire. Reuters says an unknown number of people were injured. Maritime Executive reports the corvette Merkury was seen on its side and cargo ship Ascalon was also attacked - not officially confirmed. Nobody has claimed it.

stories.headline: Search on for [missing Jordanian sailor] after Hormuz strike
stories.summary: The UAE and Oman are searching for a Jordanian seafarer missing after an ADNOC Logistics tanker was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz. The National says 11 crew were injured and the rest evacuated. JMIC says seven oil tankers have been hit since 16 November, three near Oman on 20-21 November. Iran's mine claims are not confirmed.

stories.headline: Fire on OceanJet 168 - [326 passengers rescued]
stories.summary: Around 326 passengers were rescued after a fire broke out on the fast craft OceanJet 168 in the Philippines. The ferry was sailing from Cebu Port to Ormoc Port. The Philippine Red Cross said the fire was brought under control and passengers moved to a rescue vessel. The Coast Guard is towing the craft back to Cebu.

stories.headline: IMO backs [Red Sea coastguard task force] against piracy
stories.summary: The IMO has endorsed a coastguard-led task force of about 22 nations against piracy and smuggling in the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden and West Indian Ocean. Members include Saudi Arabia, Djibouti and Yemen. Houthi attacks were cited as a cause of renewed piracy. IMO's Damien Chevallier said there is no price on the life of any seafarer.

stories.headline: US ports face [thousands of cyber attacks] daily
stories.summary: Hackers are running a growing campaign against US ports and cargo ships, with thousands of attempted attacks each day, the Financial Times reports. A wave of breaches has hit ports, oil tankers and shipping firms. The attackers are described as cybercriminals and groups linked to hostile states. No victims were named in the report.

stories.headline: MISC books [five LNG carriers] at Hudong-Zhonghua
stories.summary: GTT has won the tank design order for five new LNG carriers from China's Hudong-Zhonghua Shipbuilding. The owner is Malaysia's MISC. Each ship will carry 174,000 cubic metres using GTT's NO96 Super+ membrane system. Deliveries are planned between late 2029 and the third quarter of 2030. No contract price was given.

stories.headline: Gulf Energy Maritime tied to [four LR1 tankers]
stories.summary: Dubai's Gulf Energy Maritime is reported to have ordered up to four 74,000 dwt LR1 product tankers at K Shipbuilding's Jinhae yard. Market sources put the deal at about $264m, or $66m each, with delivery around 2029. The yard has not named the buyer, so GEM's role is not confirmed. GEM already has 10 ships on order.

stories.headline: SCI tenders [22 ships worth $3.2bn]
stories.summary: Shipping Corporation of India has issued a tender for 22 ships worth up to $3.2 billion. It covers eight 88,000 cbm VLGCs for IOC, BPCL and HPCL, twelve container ships and two 155,000 dwt Suezmax tankers. Foreign yards must invest in India or share technology to qualify. It is a tender, not yet a contract.
